title: feat(sharing): a share or sharing rule on a public object reaches an external member of the record's organization
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao9sUfiwLBMYyhPAkzpzFo9P)_

Closes #25549

Clause-②: yes (widening: the grant door and the materialiser admit one recipient population on effective-public objects)
Metadata-protocol: semantic

Letter A of the ruling on #25549 (record 6377844010, re-recorded 6378238137 after Tesla's item-by-item approval of 2026-10-24T01:28Z). An external member (`sys_member.role` exactly `external`) meets an owner-only floor on every object since #25541, so on a public object a share is how it reaches one record. The D7 pre-flight still refused that share as one "no gate would consult". This PR makes that verdict read the recipient's population.

## What changes

| Item | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| The verdict | `plugin-sharing` `sharing-service.ts` `inertGrantReason(object, recipient?)` | On an effective-`public` object with a real `owner_id` (not a federated phantom anchor), a `user` recipient whose `sys_member.role` in the record's organization is exactly `external` is admitted. Every other recipient keeps the 422 `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED`, now worded "consulted only for an external member of the record's organization, and the recipient is not one". `controlled_by_parent` (ADR-0111 D7.2), owner-less, phantom-anchor and bypass objects are refused for every recipient, as before. |
| Where it is asked | `grant()` | The object half stays first and caller-free. The recipient half runs on both paths after the organization is resolved (the rule's threaded organization, else the record's; the record's, else the session's for a direct grant). On the direct path it runs after the D1 management check, so a caller who cannot manage the record learns nothing about the recipient. No organization resolved is refused with its own named reason. |
| The population test | `isExternalMemberIn` | The stage-1 doors' test (`isExternalMembershipRole` in plugin-auth): a `sys_member` row in that organization whose role list is exactly `external`. Mirrored locally, since plugin-sharing does not depend on plugin-auth. |
| Rule materialisation | `sharing-rule-service.ts` | The per-recipient refusal is marked (`isInternalRecipientRefusal`), and all three passes (`reconcile`, `reconcileForRecord`, `reconcileRuleForUser`) skip that recipient instead of aborting. A pass that skipped any carries one `note` line on its result and logs the count once (`[sharing-rule] internal recipients skipped on a public object`). Every other D7 refusal still aborts the rule's pass, as before. |
| Lint | `validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts` | `sharing-rule-object-not-shareable` on a public anchor drops from `error` to `warning`: "so the rule is effective for external recipients only". The `controlled_by_parent` arm stays an `error`. The `os explain` entry says when to keep the rule and when to change the object's `sharingModel`. |
| Docs | `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` | One paragraph under "External principals". `permissions/index.mdx` and the app-crm comment said the rule "fails the build"; both now say what it does. |
| Changeset | `.changeset/25549-external-share-public-object.md` | `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, with both declaration lines. |

### How the rule's report surfaces (measured)

`POST /api/v1/sharing/rules/:idOrName/evaluate` answers `evaluateRule`'s return value unfiltered (`sharing-routes.ts`, `res.json(result)`), so the `note` reaches the admin who evaluates a rule. The boot backfill, the write hooks and the re-grant queues read only the counts, so for them the log line is the report. `note` is declared on plugin-sharing's own `SharingRuleReconcilePassResult`, not on the spec's `SharingRuleEvaluationResult`.

## Verification (head `a1260e57`)

- `plugin-sharing`, `system-caller-inert-grant.test.ts`, new block (9 cases): an external recipient is admitted, its row carries the record's organization and `buildReadFilter` for that external returns exactly that record; an internal recipient gets `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED:` and no row; a user external in org B and a member of org A is refused on an org A record, and the reverse user is admitted; a role list `external,member` is refused; a system caller gets the same two answers; a caller without management rights gets `PERMISSION_DENIED` first; a team rule expanding to one external and one staff member on two gold records writes two rows for the external, `grantsRefused: 0`, the note, and one log line with `skipped: 2`; a rule to externals only has no note; an owner-less public object still refuses an external.
- The #8207 pins in the same file: the rule-pass refusal block now covers the four object classes that still abort, and a new case pins that a rule on the public object with an internal recipient mints nothing and carries the note.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck` exit 0; the suite: 55/55 files, 1233 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` exit 0; the suite: 158/158 files, 7237 tests passed.
- Dogfood, `external-member-directory.dogfood.test.ts` on a showcase boot, two new cases: the owner POSTs a share of one `showcase_invoice` (`public_read_write`) to an external over `/data/showcase_invoice/ID/shares` and gets 201 with the organization stamped; the external read zero invoices before and exactly that one after. The same share to an ordinary member answers 422 with `error.code` `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED`, and no row is written. The file: 13/13. `tsc --noEmit` on the dogfood package exit 0.
- Ablation (committed fix first, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): `if (recipient === 'external') return null;` replaced so the external arm returns a reason. Anchor 1 to 0, blob c1f616f5 to 5d5c8c31; the file went red, 8 failed of 33; restored, blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `a1260e57` derived 104 families; each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe. First sweep: 101 exit 0, 3 exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: the pinned control commit absent from the shallow clone for `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`; no `client-react` dist for `check:skill-examples`; workspace dists for `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`). After fetching that commit and a locked workspace build, all three re-ran exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 104 derived, 104 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

## Acceptance notes

- **The two confidence gaps.** The REST door and the rule evaluator both have the organization at hand: `grant()` resolves it on both paths before writing (commit 3f64fe6c6), and the recipient half reads it from there. When neither path resolves one, the grant is refused with a named reason, not judged against the session's organization.
- **Error order on a public object.** For a direct grant on a public object the 422 now comes after the D1 management pre-flight, so a caller who may not manage the record gets 403/404 where it used to get 422. That is deliberate (the population is only read for an authorized caller). On every other object the order is unchanged.
- **Existing inert rows.** A `source: 'rule'` row for an internal recipient on a public object, minted by an older build, is still left standing by a pass when its level is unchanged; it is never consulted for that recipient.
- **Spec contract docblock.** `ISharingService.grant`'s docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` still says a share on a public object "enforces nothing". It is outside this claim's file surface and is left for the seat to route with the ADR-0111 line drafted in the os-dev-report.
- **ADR-0111 D7.** The dated line is Tier H and is not in this PR; its draft is in the os-dev-report on the card.
